name: Isothermal process
statement: In an isothermal process the temperature stays constant, so an ideal gas has ΔU = 0 and all the heat absorbed is returned as work (Q = W).

name: Adiabatic process
statement: In an adiabatic process no heat is exchanged with the surroundings, so Q = 0 and ΔU = −W.

name: First law of thermodynamics
statement: The change in the internal energy of a closed system equals the heat added to it minus the work it does on its surroundings: ΔU = Q − W.
aliases: energy conservation for heat and work

name: Internal energy of an ideal gas
statement: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on its temperature, not on its pressure or volume.

name: State function
statement: A state function is a property whose value depends only on the current state of the system, not on the path taken to reach that state.

name: Heat
statement: Heat is energy transferred between two systems because of a temperature difference between them.

name: Work done by an expanding gas
statement: When a gas expands by ΔV against a constant external pressure p, it does work W = pΔV on its surroundings.

name: Isobaric process
statement: An isobaric process takes place at constant pressure, so the work done by the gas is W = pΔV and Q = ΔH.

name: Isochoric process
statement: In an isochoric process the volume is constant, so no pV work is done and ΔU = Q.

name: Molar heat capacity at constant volume
statement: The molar heat capacity at constant volume, C_V, is the heat needed to raise the temperature of one mole by one kelvin without changing the volume.

name: Mayer's relation
statement: For an ideal gas the molar heat capacities at constant pressure and constant volume differ by the gas constant: C_p = C_V + R.

name: Ideal gas law
statement: An ideal gas obeys pV = nRT, relating pressure, volume, amount of substance and absolute temperature.
aliases: equation of state of an ideal gas

name: Heat engine
statement: A heat engine takes heat from a hot reservoir, converts part of it into work and rejects the remainder to a cold reservoir.

name: Thermal efficiency
statement: The thermal efficiency of a heat engine is the work output divided by the heat absorbed from the hot reservoir: η = W/Q_h = 1 − Q_c/Q_h.

name: Kelvin–Planck statement
statement: No device operating in a cycle can absorb heat from a single reservoir and convert all of it into work.

name: Clausius statement
statement: Heat does not flow spontaneously from a colder body to a hotter body.

name: Carnot engine
statement: A Carnot engine is a reversible engine working between two reservoirs; no engine between the same reservoirs can be more efficient.

name: Carnot efficiency
statement: The efficiency of a Carnot engine is η = 1 − T_c/T_h, with both temperatures measured on the kelvin scale.

name: Entropy
statement: For a reversible exchange of heat at temperature T, the entropy of a system changes by ΔS = Q_rev/T.

name: Entropy of an isolated system
statement: The entropy of an isolated system never decreases; it stays constant only for reversible processes.
aliases: second law in terms of entropy

name: Reversible process
statement: A reversible process is one that can be run backwards, restoring both the system and its surroundings, which requires it to proceed through equilibrium states.

name: Zeroth law of thermodynamics
statement: If two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other.

name: Absolute temperature
statement: Absolute temperature is measured in kelvin, with absolute zero as the lowest possible temperature; it is the scale used in the ideal gas law.

name: Thermal reservoir
statement: A thermal reservoir is a system so large that its temperature does not change when it exchanges heat.
